name: Hay Head Wood Wild Garlic
short_description: Limestone woodland carpeted in spring garlic.
description: The ancient semi-natural woodland at Hay Head Nature Reserve produces a magnificent display of wild garlic each spring, with the densest picking along the damp hollows near the old limestone workings.

name: Chasewater Country Park Bilberries
short_description: Heathland bilberries on the reservoir edge.
description: The open heathland surrounding Chasewater reservoir supports a healthy population of bilberry plants, with the best picking on the southern and western heath margins in midsummer.

name: Walsall Arboretum Blackberries
description: The wilder hedgerow margins and shrubbery edges of Walsall Arboretum yield good quantities of blackberries each late summer, particularly along the northern boundary near the boating lake.

name: Barr Beacon Sloes and Rosehips
short_description: Hilltop hedgerow harvest with panoramic views.
description: The exposed hedgerows and scrubby field margins around Barr Beacon are laden with blackthorn sloes and dog rose hips each autumn, some of the best in the borough.

name: Aldridge Community Orchard
short_description: Local heritage varieties in the heart of Aldridge.
description: A community-planted orchard near Aldridge town centre featuring traditional Midlands apple, pear, and plum varieties, maintained by volunteers and open for public picking throughout autumn.

name: Incredible Edible Walsall Town Centre Planters
short_description: Edible street planters in the town centre.
description: Community growing planters located around the town centre and St Matthew's Quarter featuring culinary herbs, kale, and salad leaves for passers-by to pick freely.

name: Pelsall Common Blackberries and Elder
short_description: Open common with productive scrub margins.
description: The bracken and scrub edges of Pelsall Common provide good late summer blackberrying and elderberry picking, with well-worn footpaths making the common easy to explore.

name: Shire Oak Park Hazelnuts
short_description: Ancient hedgerow nuts near the old park.
description: Hazel bushes in the mature hedgerows and woodland remnants around Shire Oak Park produce a reliable nut crop each autumn, best gathered on dry September mornings.

name: Rushall Canal Corridor Elderflower and Berries
description: Elder bushes are abundant along the Rushall Canal towpath, offering elderflower for cordial in early summer and heavy elderberry clusters by September.

name: Bloxwich Park Wild Plums and Damsons
short_description: Hedgerow tree fruits in north Walsall.
description: Wild plum and damson trees grow in the hedgerows and rough ground bordering Bloxwich Park and the surrounding estate lanes — a traditional Black Country hedgerow find.

name: Clayhanger Wetlands Wild Greens
short_description: Wetland margins rich in edible greens.
description: The reed-fringed wetland margins of Clayhanger SSSI support watermint, wild sorrel, and patches of water pepper along the boardwalk edges throughout the growing season.

name: Brownhills Common Sweet Chestnuts
short_description: Mature chestnuts on the common edge.
description: A row of mature sweet chestnut trees on the wooded boundary of Brownhills Common produces a generous crop of nuts each October, easily gathered from the ground after the first frosts.

name: Darlaston Community Growing Planters
description: Raised community planters near the town centre and local shops grow seasonal herbs and vegetables, maintained by local residents and free for the community to harvest.

name: Streetly Wood Wild Garlic
short_description: Ancient woodland garlic on the Sutton border.
description: The semi-ancient broadleaf woodland of Streetly Wood on the Walsall and Sutton Coldfield boundary is carpeted with wild garlic in spring, with some of the most accessible picking off the main woodland trails.

name: Willenhall Memorial Park Rosehips and Haws
description: The boundary hedgerows of Willenhall Memorial Park are rich with dog rose and hawthorn, giving a reliable autumn crop of rosehips and haws ideal for making syrups, jellies, and hedgerow gin.
